attributes.assistantPrompt: This is my plant-care spreadsheet, exported as `enchantment/houseplants.csv`. Make it into an app: one card per plant, each showing when it next needs water, and a dashboard that lists which plants are due today or overdue, grouped by room. Show me the dashboard. Don't ask me any follow-up questions; decide the details yourself.
followUpPrompts: I just watered the Boston fern and the snake plant. Record that, and add a new plant: a Golden Pothos (Epipremnum aureum) in the Kitchen, in medium indirect light, that needs water every 7 days and was watered today. Show me the dashboard again.
attributes.successCriteria:
The CSV's dates are set relative to the day the run starts, so the expectations below hold on any run date. "Today" below is the run day: the Calathea's `last_watered` date in the workspace snapshot's copy of `enchantment/houseplants.csv`, plus one day. Don't take it from the result's start time, which is in UTC and can be a different day from the one the CSV was written on.

Task A (turn the spreadsheet into an app):

A1. A plant definition with typed fields: the watering interval is a number and the last-watered date is a `DateField` (or `DateTimeField`), not a string. The next-water date (last watered plus the interval) is a `computeVia`, not a stored field.

A2. All 12 rows of `enchantment/houseplants.csv` exist as plant instances, each with its name, species, room, light, interval and last-watered date as the file gives them. None is missing, added or merged.

A3. A dashboard finds the plants with a query or `linksToMany` (not a copy of their data) and lists exactly the six plants due today or overdue: Boston Fern (Bathroom), Snake Plant (Bedroom), Fiddle-Leaf Fig and Spider Plant (Living Room), Peace Lily (Office) and Aloe Vera (Kitchen). Due-ness is computed from the current date when the card renders, not hard-coded. A card that takes the current date in UTC rather than local time passes only if its list is right for the run day; say so in the analysis either way. The list is grouped by room, and the dashboard is open on screen with no error boundary.

A4. `enchantment/houseplants.csv` is unchanged.

Task B (use the app):

B1. The Boston Fern's and the Snake Plant's last-watered dates are today, and the dashboard no longer lists them as due: it lists the other four. Only those two existing instances changed.

B2. A Golden Pothos instance exists with the species, room (Kitchen), light, a 7-day interval and today's date. It is not listed as due.

B3. The follow-up is data only: no definition was rewritten for it, and no instance was deleted or recreated. The dashboard is open on screen again with no error boundary.

Z. Every tool call applied or was repaired by the model, the assistant did not ask a question or wait for confirmation before acting, and the whole flow took at most 20 turns.

cardInfo.name: Enchantment: plant spreadsheet to a tracker app
cardInfo.summary: The workspace starts with one static file, a plant-care spreadsheet exported as `enchantment/houseplants.csv` with 12 plants. The first prompt asks to turn it into an app, a card per plant with its next watering date and a dashboard of the plants due today or overdue, by room. The second prompt records two waterings and adds a plant. This eval tests whether the selected models can upgrade a spreadsheet into typed cards with a computed field and a live dashboard, then use the app by editing its data.
cardInfo.notes: The CSV comes from the `houseplants` seed script, with each plant's last watering a fixed number of days before the run starts, so the same six plants are due on every run.
